riscos.descricao: Código gerado pode conter fraquezas conhecidas (CWEs) exploráveis; mesmo o modelo com melhor desempenho (GPT-4) produziu programas funcionais exploráveis em proporção que o estudo descreve como quase metade.

Preâmbulos de segurança aumentam a complexidade do código e reduzem a correção, com desvio dos critérios de entrada e saída e código não funcional, sobretudo quando o modelo deve gerar código e detectar vulnerabilidades ao mesmo tempo.

riscos.descricao: Variabilidade significativa das saídas, mesmo em temperaturas baixas, levando a comportamentos diferentes nos testes unitários.

Modelos mais novos têm tempo de resposta maior e estratégias de chain prompting exigem requisições extras à API, tornando-as menos eficientes em recursos; tempos apresentados só graficamente (Fig. 2), sem valores impressos.

Salvaguardas embutidas podem recusar pedidos de endurecimento ou análise de segurança: Gemini 1.0 deu erros de salvaguarda sem saída utilizável em 12.5% dos programas gerados, sempre em entradas Id, e recusas tornam incerto o tempo de requisições.

citacoes.trecho: To address this concern, our research examines different prompt types for shaping responses from code generation tasks to produce safer outputs.
These inputs are then paired with different contexts, roles, and identification prompts intended to improve security.
Our findings show that the inclusion of appropriate guidance reduces vulnerabilities in generated code, with the choice of model having the most significant effect.
We examine the most popular recent commercial offerings, including OpenAI’s ChatGPT-3.5 and 4.5, Anthropic’s Claude Instant and Opus, and Google’s Gemini 1.0.
Specifically, adding guidance to harden programs leads to increased complexity that may introduce compilation and logic issues.
There are ten unique security preambles used as described in Table I.
We selected three security-oriented prompt patterns based on the classifications outlined in [37].
These patterns encompass context control, role-based output, and error identification, as detailed in Table I.
We further investigated combinations of these prompts to assess if additional security emphasis influenced the outcomes.
This led to a total of 11 in possible security preambles since tests are also performed with no preamble.
The security and specification prompts are combined to create the template shown in Listing 1.
Only operational programs undergo security evaluation.
Such instances are excluded from the final security metrics.
This is accomplished through a simple search in the resulting output for the appropriate CWE identifier.
While the precise settings for many LLM web interfaces remain undisclosed, the ChatGPT API documentation states a default value of 1.0 and provides example settings of 0.8 and 0.2 [41].
The temperatures (τ) selected were τ = 0.2, 0.5, 1.0 to represent values across the range [0,1].
The total number of tests for these trials was 3630 since we evaluate across 11 security preambles, 11 CWE-inducing prompts, 3 temperatures, and perform 10 trials for each permutation.
We also tested with multiple other commercial models, specifically: GPT-4, Claude Instant, Claude Opus, and Gemini 1.0.
This led to an additional 605 test that evaluated across 11 security preambles and 11 CWE-inducing prompts but only performed single trials for each of the 5 models.
During our evaluation, we observed significant variability in output.
The average accuracies and standard deviations were calculated across all 30 trials to ensure statistically significant findings [42].
Also, a simple chain prompting strategy that introduced each prompt type of security guidance sequentially was tested.
This included first giving the program specification with no guidance, then the full role guidance, and finally the vulnerability identification direction.
As shown in Fig. 3, the use of security-focused prompts generally led to enhanced security measures.
The All prompt, encompassing all prior directives, produced the maximum number of programs resistant to exploitation.
As seen in Fig. 3, integrating security-specific prompts often compromised program accuracy, defined as the percentage of programs passing the corresponding unit test.
This decline in program correctness was particularly pronounced when the LLM was tasked with both code generation and vulnerability detection.
The notable exception was Gemini 1.0 which frequently gave safeguard errors and provided no usable output.
This accounted for 12.5% of the generated programs for Gemini 1.0 and always corresponded with the Id entries from Table I, although inconsistently.
However, these strategies increase complexity and require extra API requests, rendering them less resource-efficient as shown in the collected timings.
However, no consistent method to enhance security without compromising program correctness was identified.
ChatGPT-4 displayed the best performance across all code-generation measures, but almost half of the working programs were exploitable.
Multiple trials were run for each unique combination of prompts and temperatures to collect statistics on the findings [42].
Servers for each model were tested using the ping program beforehand to determine network latency resulting in response times between 12.6 ± 0.1 ms.

Template, preâmbulos, especificações, testes unitários e número de trials são descritos, mas as temperaturas divergem entre texto e Fig. 4, a regra de exclusão de inconclusivos é ambígua e o subconjunto dos testes de tempo não é dimensionado.
